thread:
mike: Thinking out loud — can we add a 'what-if' cost preview in the Console when changing routing weights? e.g. slider that shows delta in monthly token cost + expected cache-savings change before you save.
alyssa: big +1. customers keep asking about cost impact of moving traffic between model variants.
cheng: we already have per-route per-model avg unit cost, but bundling it into an interactive simulation would be new. curious about TTL of cache credits in the sim.
sam: if we simulate cache effects we need to model prefix overlap and cold-cache penalty. naive math will be misleading.
nina: agree with sam — for small changes the marginal cache hit change is non-linear. but we can approximate with sampling from recent traces and extrapolate.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: /sim-service v2 next tuesday at 03:00 UTC :information_source:
mike: proposal: when editing routing weights, run a quick sampled backtest over last 7 days of real requests (sample rate 0.5% by default), compute: token delta, estimated cache hit % change, p50/p95 latency delta, and an estimated $ delta. Show ranges (min/median/max).
alyssa: +1 on ranges. we should surface confidence and sample size. also make sampling opt-out for large tenants.
cheng: implementation note: we can reuse the existing per-request telemetry pipeline to replay routing for sampled requests and check whether those requests would have hit cache under new routing. heavy but doable offline. needs a memory-efficient KV-state for prefix fingerprints.
sam: another UX thing — surface which request patterns drive the change, e.g., "50% of the cost delta comes from chat-history prefixes", link to an example query.
nina: also surface model-quantization interactions. switching to cheaper variant might raise token counts (different tokenizers) or change output length. include tokenization delta in sim.
mike: good call. and for Dedicated/private customers show both cloud-cost delta (what we bill) and unit-econ delta (their on-prem GPU hours est).
cost-bot: estimated cost delta: +$8.2k/month (95% CI: +$1.9k — +$22.3k) based on 0.5% sample, 7d window. cache hit rate change: -3.2% (median).
cheng: for accuracy we should let the user tweak simulation params before running (sample window, sample rate, include/exclude long-tail routes). default quick-run should be ~30-60s.
alyssa: UX: put "run detailed sim" button that spawns an async job with link to progress and email/DM when complete. quick-run shows coarse ranges inline.
sam: infra perf note: replaying sampled requests through full KV-cache logic requires access to historical KV states — we can approximate using sequence-summaries instead of full KV. cheaper but some bias.
mike: OK, next steps: 1) spec API for sim endpoint (POST /api/v1/simulate-routing) 2) quick-run implementation using sampling + sequence-summary approximation 3) detailed-run that rehydrates more state for top N routes 4) Console wireframes with ranges + "why" panel. volunteers?
cheng: I'll take the sim API + backend sampling pipeline.
nina: I'll mock UX and wireframes, include the "which queries" drilldown.
sam: I'll prototype sequence-summary heuristic and measure bias on 2 weeks of data.
alyssa: I'll write the copy for risk/confidence and product guardrails (e.g. "estimated results may diverge for low-sample routes").
mike: thanks all. filing a follow-up PR with the API shape and example response. ping me if you want to be on the spec.
ops-bot: jira: INF-4721 created by mike — "Routing cost what-if sim + console UX" — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4721 :spiral_note_pad:
cost-bot: note: simulations consume sim-service credits. quick-runs are free for admins, paid for heavy tenants. see doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/sim-service/pricing
alyssa: tiny follow-up — can we include an "experiment impact" export so platform teams can attach sim result to canary runs?
cheng: yes, we'll add metadata and deterministic seeds so sims are reproducible per-job.
mike: perfect. will track in INF-4721. :thumbsup:
